name: Coding Practice with Python
description: A hands-on introduction to Python for the inventory and data work at Riverbend.
about: Everyone at Riverbend ends up peering at the same tall spreadsheet sooner or later. This course is the small amount of Python that makes that less painful: reading files, checking a value, printing an answer. It is deliberately short — a prospect is a few minutes of practice away from a working script, not a course in computer science.
learnings: Run Python code in the browser; read and check inventory-style values; turn a business question into a short script; submit the final check-in for review.

updates.title: New course: Coding Practice with Python
updates.content: Added after the warehouse team asked for a short, practical way to try Python without installing anything. Every example uses real Riverbend data.

chapters.name: Getting started
chapters.description: What Python is doing here, and why Riverbend reaches for it.

activities.name: Why Riverbend uses Python
body: p:A dashboard tells you what the numbers are. Python tells you what happens when you act on them: which order to prioritise, which SKU to reorder, which rows in a report are actually outliers. Most of that amounts to small scripts like the one below, run and thrown away.
p:You do not need to be a programmer. You need the same skill you already use on a spreadsheet — asking a question of data — with a print statement instead of a sum.
p:The editor below runs real Python in the browser. Press run, read the output, then change the message and run it again. Nothing is installed on your machine.

codePlayground.starter_code:
order = "Order 4192 is ready to ship"
print(order)
codePlayground.description: Run this snippet, then change the message to your own team's name and run it again.

a: Acting on data with small scripts

body: info:Every code block in this course is marked by the editor on-screen — a learner can type in it, run it, and get feedback before moving on.

activities.name: The parts of a Python script
Your first script
body: p:Almost every script you write here does the same three things: read a value into a variable, decide something about it, and print the result. Run this one with the green button and watch the answer appear in the panel below the editor.
p:Then change the 21 to your own number and run it again — the output will follow it.

codePlayground.description: A variable, a function and a print. Read the output, tweak the number, run again.

body: p:Below the editor is the output panel. A green tick means your program printed what the test expected; red shows the difference. If the code hangs, the stop button cancels it.

ul: The editor runs server-side, so your script sees nothing on your machine.
Output is compared with expectations, but any output is shown to you either way.
Re-run as often as you like — there is no penalty for experimenting.

activities.name: A real inventory task
body: p:Every Monday the warehouse sends a list of SKUs with units on hand. A SKU is worth reordering when its stock has fallen below 40 units. Write a script that checks the two sample SKUs below and prints the name and stock for the one that needs reordering.

codePlayground.description: This one is the real thing: check which SKU needs reordering and print its name and stock.
hints: Iterate the dictionary and print only rows where units is below 40.

body: p:That is the whole course in miniature: read the data, apply a rule, print the answer. Whatever else you automate at Riverbend, it will be this shape.

a: CW-2271, because it has the most stock
